The Department of Pediatric Oncology, Hematology and Clinical Immunology at the University Hospital Düsseldorf (UKD) at the Heinrich Heine University (HHU), headed by Prof. Dr. Arndt Borkhardt, is one of the leading clinical centers for the diagnosis and treatment of childhood cancer in Germany. The clinic is part of the University Tumor Center (UTZ) at the UKD and the Center for Integrative Oncology Aachen-Bonn-Cologne-Düsseldorf (CIO-ABCD), which is funded by the German Cancer Aid. It is a founding partner of the German Consortium for Translational Cancer Research (DKTK) Essen-Düsseldorf and participates in international research consortia and study groups. The clinic operates a fully equipped research laboratory (safety level 1 and 2 according to the Genetic Engineering/Biotechnology Ordinance, including a GMP, next generation sequencing, flow cytometry, life cell imaging, and high-throughput drug testing facility) with 5 research groups and >30 staff working in an interdisciplinary manner on the fundamentals of childhood cancer and in the field of therapy optimization. We are seeking a highly motivated and creative PhD Student to join our research program in the field of amino acid homeostasis and cancer metabolism, with an anticipated start date of 02/2027. The successful candidate will work on the ERC-funded project “POWERFUL” (Deciphering how cancer cells fuel themselves to advance personalized treatment strategies).The PhD student will take a leading role in understanding how cancer cells sense and respond to amino acid availability, and how to translate this knowledge into precision-based treatment strategies. This position requires scientific independence and the opportunity to contribute intellectually to experimental design, data interpretation, and publication strategy. The candidate will employ and further develop advanced experimental models and methodologies, including organoid systems, patient-derived xenografts (PDXs), CRISPR/Cas9-based genome editing, multiparameter flow cytometry, confocal microscopy, FRET assays, protein interaction and signaling assays, as well as in vitro and in vivo drug screening approaches.Candidates should have a very good understanding of and experience with standard molecular biology techniques including but not limited to tissue culture, genome editing, FACS analysis, confocal microscopy, immunoblot, and PCR/qPCR. Experience with animal models is a plus (as is FELASA B certification). Willingness to learn and work with murine experimental models is a fundamental requirement. - Master in natural sciences or related field- Solid experience with cancer models (e.g. organoids, PDXs) and drug-response studies- expertise in molecular and cellular biology techniques, including mammalian tissue culture, genome editing, FACS/flow cytometry, confocal microscopy, immunoblotting, and PCR/qPCR.- Excellent capability to develop new aspects and projects within the given research focus- Excellent written and spoken English language skills, German language skills are a plus- Organizational and project management experience- Willingness to cooperate and ability to work in a team- Experience in working with animals (FELASA B) is a plus, willingness to work with animals a requisite Remuneration is based on TV-L in pay grade 13 (65%), taking into account all previous periods of employment. The employment contract will be concluded with Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf.Applications from women are expressly welcome. Women will be given preferential consideration if they have the same qualifications, skills, and professional performance, unless there are reasons related to a male competitor that outweigh this. Severely disabled applicants will be given preferential consideration if they have the same qualifications.We offer:- challenging and varied tasks in a committed, interdisciplinary team- attractive opportunities for further training and development- opportunity to travel and ...

The German Diabetes Center (DDZ) is the Leibniz Institute for Diabetes Research at Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf. The DDZ is an interdisciplinary research center linking molecular and cell biological basic with clinical and epidemiological research approaches. The DDZ has the aim to develop new approaches for prevention, early detection and diagnosis of diabetes mellitus and to improve therapy and treatment of its complications.The Institute for Clinical Diabetology (Director: Prof. Dr. Michael Roden) is looking for anEpidemiologist (postdoc - m/f/d) We are searching for a candidate with (1) a doctoral degree in epidemiology, (bio)statistics or a comparable discipline, (2) the ability to work in an interdisciplinary manner with physicians and life scientists, and (3) knowledge of epidemiological methodology and statistical analysis systems (e.g. SAS or R). In addition, excellent writing and communication skills in English are required. Experience in the analysis of proteomics data would be desirable.The project will be a collaboration between the research group Inflammation (Prof. Dr. Christian Herder) and the Clinical Study Center (Prof. Dr. Robert Wagner, PD Dr. Oana-Patricia Zaharia) at DDZ. Tasks include planning epidemiological analyses within different cohort studies, performing statistical analyses in projects related to the link between inflammation, diabetes and cardiovascular complications, and communicating results in conferences and publications. The coordination of projects with internal and external partners is important as the position will be linked to projects with the Department of Cardiology, Pulmonology and Vascular Medicine at the Medical Faculty, Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf.An exciting and diversified fulltime job in a multidisciplinary team. The project should start on the earliest possible start date with a 3-year-contract.A salary as based on qualification and experience according to TV-L in its current version for North Rhine-Westphalia.Family-friendly working conditions and equal gender policy. Since May 2011, the DDZ is a “Career and Family” audit-acknowledged center.Women are especially encouraged to apply, and in the case of equal qualification will be given preference. Similarly, persons with disabilities will be given preference.

The group of Prof. Dr. Eva Nowack, Institute of Microbial Cell Biology at Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf is looking forPostdoc (m/f/d) in Endosymbiosis ResearchJob-ID: J000000668Working hours: Full timeLocation: DüsseldorfStart date: 01.01.2027Limited until: 31.12.2028Apply till: 21.10.2026Payment group: EGr. 13 TV-LOrganization: MathematischNaturwissenschaftliche FakultätJob Category: science / research / teach To support our ongoing research, we are seeking a highly motivated Postdoctoral Researcher to join our team. Our group is an enthusiastic and collaborative team of cell and evolutionary biologists investigating the evolutionary transition from bacterial endosymbionts to eukaryotic organelles. We seek to understand, at the mechanistic level, how protists interact with permanent bacterial endosymbionts and how these associations evolve toward organellogenesis. To address these questions, we combine state-of-the-art omics approaches with detailed molecular biological and protein biochemical experimentation. As model systems, we have established the photosynthetic amoeba Paulinella chromatophora and the symbiont-harboring trypanosomatid Angomonas deanei and related species in the laboratory. Our work has provided exciting insights into organellogenesis and enabled us to develop novel tools for dissecting the molecular and cellular biology of host-symbiont interactions (see e.g., Morales et al. (2023) Curr Biol. doi: 10.1016/j.cub.2022.11.020.; Sørensen et al. (2024) FEBS J. doi: 10.1111/febs.17356; Maurya et al. (2025) Science Adv. doi: 10.1126/sciadv.adp8518; Klimenko et al. (2025) Plant Phys. doi: 10.1093/plphys/kiaf504; Hammond et al. (2026) Nat Commun. doi: 10.1038/s41467-026-70084-0.). The successful candidate will contribute to a current project at the heart of our research program, with the opportunity to shape the project in part according to their scientific interests, expertise, and strengths. The position will also involve a limited amount of undergraduate teaching in German [4 contact hours (Semesterwochenstunden) per week], providing an opportunity to contribute to the training of the next generation of biologists.A PhD in biology, biochemistry or a related areaAn excellent academic track recordResearch experience in microbiology or cell biology, genetic engineering, and advanced microscopy techniquesExperience with organelle biology, symbioses or protistology is a plusA strong motivation in experimental work, literature search and scientific writingReadiness to work independently and as a team player in an interdisciplinary, international teamFluency (oral and written) in English and GermanProactive character, creativity, communication and presentation skills, excellent organization and analytical skillsThe position is initially limited for a period of 2 years with the possibility of extension.
